assumptions.statement: To prove 'the application starts' on a database created from main, the tests start a second application host via Factory.WithWebHostBuilder with only postgres:connectionString overridden, and let the host's own startup path (DbContextAppInitializer) run the migrations.
assumptions.default_chosen: Second host from the shared fixture (same config and test services). The connection string is overridden through an in-memory configuration source added after the fixture's own source.
assumptions.rationale: This is the startup path the trace-auditor asked for (findings 1-4 and 1-5). PostgresOptions are bound lazily (Shared.Infrastructure/Postgres/Extensions.cs:95-98), so the override reaches every module DbContext. No shared infrastructure change is needed.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If the host ever reads the connection string eagerly at registration time, the second host would silently use the shared database. The AC-14 test guards against this: it asserts pending migrations exist before the host starts and none remain after. The AC-9 read only succeeds because the group read model exists only in the upgraded database.

assumptions.statement: The create-resource modal spec replaces GroupContextStore with a stub that exposes only a schemas signal. It uses the real ResourcesApiService with HttpTestingController.
assumptions.default_chosen: Stub the store with schemas only. Run the real component and the real API service, and assert on the HTTP request body.
assumptions.rationale: The modal reads only store.schemas (create-resource-modal.component.ts:51). Under test is the payload the screen builds and sends to POST /resources/instances, so the service and HTTP layer stay real.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If the modal later reads more of the store, the stub needs more members and the spec fails loudly at run time. Nothing would pass by accident.
